title: Livox SDK2 LiDAR definitions (include/livox_lidar_def.h)
title_short: Livox SDK2 point cloud and IMU data packet
license_line: struct member names, types and array sizes only; MIT License
extra_sources: Livox SDK2 samples/livox_lidar_quick_start/main.cpp at the same commit: which item struct each data_type value carries
Livox wiki, Mid-360 Ethernet protocol page (livox-wiki-en.readthedocs.io): the byte order only

packet.name: point
convention: A message of this format is the UDP payload of one Livox SDK2 point cloud or IMU data packet:
the header struct `LivoxLidarEthernetPacket` of `include/livox_lidar_def.h` without its
flexible last member, then `dot_num` items of the struct that `data_type` names. The UDP
datagram, its ports and the device discovery are the transport's, not this pack's.
evidence: Which struct each `data_type` carries: the header's enum `LivoxLidarPointDataType` names the
values, and the SDK's quick-start sample casts the packet's `data` to
for the values 1, 2 and 3 and reads `dot_num` of them. For 0 (IMU) the sample has no cast;
the pack takes `LivoxLidarImuRawPoint`, the header's only IMU sample struct, by its name.
Byte order: the header does not state it. The SDK reads a received packet by casting its
bytes onto the packed struct with no byte swap, so the wire order is the host's of the
machines it runs on; Livox's public protocol page for the Mid-360 states that the protocol
data is little-endian. Only that fact is taken from the page, which states no licence.
bind_note: None. The Cartesian points are in millimetres (high) or centimetres (low) in the LiDAR's own
frame and the spherical points are range and angles from it: no shared key has that
meaning. The packet's timestamp is 8 bytes whose epoch depends on `time_type`; the header
declares it as bytes, so it is 8 raw keys. Every field is a raw key of module `livox`.

not_mapped: a raw key, written on encode as the entity holds it: a field that counts the whole message is not in the fixed `bits` layout (`length … whole` is sequential only, and this packet's count field is not adjacent to its items)
a raw key, not checked on decode and not computed on encode: the pack language has no CRC
the header declares `uint8_t[8]`, so the pack carries 8 byte keys; its unit and epoch depend on `time_type`
a raw integer (the header's comment gives a unit of 0.1 microsecond); no shared key has that meaning

a key-value list: a 16-bit key count, then a 16-bit reserved word, then the items. The sequential `group … count` reads its count immediately before the items, and the fixed layout has no items of varying length, so the list cannot be stated; see the report's missing additions
the control protocol (`LivoxLidarCmdPacket` with a CRC-16 over its header and a CRC-32 over its data), not data packets
`data_type` values the header does not name
